title: European jazz is high in quality and sincere
summary: European musicians play only American songs with real interest; Czech songs sounded American, and the first they asked him to learn was I'll Build a Fence Around You.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What you're really saying is that the quality of jazz music throughout Europe is extremely high.

Yes, it is and the biggest thing I want to put across is this -- their interest. They are so sincere with their playing, you know -- it's-- they shoes --old button shoes don't feel - well, it's not old / to them - they're really working at it.
And, therefore, is a major influence that this country has had on Europe.

Well, it's unbelievable. They don't play anything but American songs. Now, of course, in Czechoslovakia they asked me if I would mind playing a couple of Czech songs - well, they sounded just like American songs so it didn't make much difference--
--you know. And, then, of course I played Northern Ireland this time--
Were they a little bit surprised at the way you learned their songs?
Well, they play the same songs that I do.
Well, you said they wanted you to play a couple of Czech songs-

Well, I played all the songs that they knew - they were just all American songs, but I said the Czech songs sounded exactly like an American song-- I thought a very interesting thing, you know, the Iron Curtain

countries - as they say - the first song they wanted me to learn was -- "I'll Build a Fence Around You" --- and I got a laugh out of guys in the band when I said - that's a a hell of a title for this country-- well, anyway, it went on and I did Northern Ireland last year and it was kind of scarey at the airport and things like that but it ran into a very good band--
